key_insight: Among WC-10Co-4Cr thermal-sprayed coatings, HVOF and HVAF delivered the best wear performance, while HVAF gave the strongest corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: Selecting the spray process strongly changes coating microstructure and service performance, so process choice can be optimized for either wear-critical or corrosion-critical applications on stainless steel components.
method: WC-10Co-4Cr coatings were deposited on 304 stainless steel by APS, DS, HVOF, and HVAF.
Microstructure was compared alongside hardness, tribological response, and electrochemical corrosion behavior.
Wear tracks and corrosion metrics were used to rank coating performance across processes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports hardness of 771.4, 954.2, 1166.2, and 1162.2 HV and wear rates of 7.93, 1.51, 1.17, and 1.10 ×10^-5 mm3/N·m for APS, DS, HVOF, and HVAF, respectively, with HVAF showing the best corrosion metrics.
watch_item: Performance rankings are specific to the reported test conditions, so field service behavior may differ with load, environment, and substrate preparation.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
